messages:
Jess: @channel ACME reporting frequent 502/504s from hosted inference since ~2026-03-15T09:08Z. They say it started after a cert rollout + DNS changes. Customer attached curl showing TLS handshake timeouts. Escalating to eng-dns + eng-runtime.

Ana: we see a spike of resolver SERVFAILs around 09:09-09:12 UTC and matching upstream handshake timeouts. tagging @eng_dns. (reacted with :eyes:)

eng_dns: grabbing dig/traceroute from an edge in us-west-2. sample dig shows SERVFAIL from our forwarder 10.2.1.5:

```
$ dig +time=2 +tries=2 @10.2.1.5 api.redwood-hosted.com A
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 54321
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1
;; SERVER: 10.2.1.5#53(10.2.1.5) (UDP)
```

and a successful resolution via public DNS:

```
$ dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood-hosted.com A +short
3.120.145.22
```

Looks like internal forwarder intermittently returning SERVFAIL during zone refresh. Collecting tcpdump and netstat.

eng_runtime: runtime logs show many upstream handshake timeouts at the same time. sample: 

```
2026-03-15T09:10:07Z ERROR upstream_connect: handshake timeout after 10s for backend model-gpu-01
2026-03-15T09:10:07Z WARN fallback: switched to fallback-model-small
```

We have fallback but when prefix cache misses line up with DNS failures, requests end up hitting gateway timeouts and surface as 502s to customers.

Jess: customer curl (sanitized):

```
curl -v https://api.redwood-hosted.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>"
* Trying 3.120.145.22...
* Connected to api.redwood-hosted.com (3.120.145.22) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLS handshake timeout
* Connection failed
```

Customer: "~15% of requests get 502s, mostly on cold starts; happens across regions. we see 'tls handshake timeout' in our logs."

eng_dns: tcpdump shows a ~20-30s window where forwarder 10.2.1.5 returned SERVFAILs. Suspect forwarding VM had high CPU during our zone propagation at ~09:05. Opening infra ticket.

infra-bot: deploy: cert-rotation v2026.03.15-0904 applied to edge-control-plane at 2026-03-15T09:04:26Z by pipeline-ci.

deploy-bot: cert rotation completed, nodes reported success; no rollback.

eng_runtime: theory: cert rotation triggered rehandshakes while DNS flapped -> TLS client-hello retry loops and connection stalls -> upstream handshake timeouts -> 502 spikes. Need SNI/ALPN and TLS close reason logs to confirm.

Ana: can we reproduce externally? suggested steps:
1) dig @10.2.1.5 api.redwood-hosted.com (simulate SERVFAIL)
2) openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-hosted.com:443 -servername api.redwood-hosted.com -tls1_3 -msg
3) run a curl loop to measure TLS timeouts

eng_dns: quick repro on a canary by dropping some UDP 53 packets:

```
# drop ~20% of outgoing UDP 53
iptables -A OUTPUT -p udp --dport 53 -m statistic --mode random --probability 0.2 -j DROP
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer}\n" https://api.redwood-hosted.com/v1/health || echo curl failed; sleep 0.1; done
```

With that set, we repro ~5-12% TLS connect failures, which matches customer numbers.

Jess: customer asked for immediate mitigations. suggested short-term options:
- route their traffic to a region with healthy resolvers (us-east-1)
- enable connection pooling/keepalives for them to reduce cold-handshake exposure
- recommend client-side retry/backoff temporarily
They chose regional pin + keepalive.

eng_runtime: ops fixes we can do:
- immediate: pin customer to a pre-warmed pool to reduce cold starts
- near-term: include stable public forwarders in resolver list during zone rollouts
- long-term: stronger resolver fallback to prefer cached A records for a short duration when SERVFAIL seen

Ana: incident INC-2026-0315-01 created and paged oncall; assigning eng_dns + eng_runtime P1. ETA: mitigation update in 30m.

eng_dns: identified a forwarding resolver VM with high load; restarting it now.

eng_runtime: post-restart we see handshake timeouts drop to baseline in ~90s. Pushing a config change to reduce resolver fallback timeout from 10s -> 3s. Opening PR.

Jess: customer reports error rate down to low single digits; occasional cold-start 502s persist. They accepted remaining mitigation and will stay on pinned pool until config lands.

eng_runtime: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/inference/ops/pull/234 update resolver fallback timeout and add client_hello_retry_count metric. will canary in 10m.

infra-bot: incident linked to ticket TKT-6543 and INC-2026-0315-01.

Ana: initial postmortem notes: root cause = forwarding resolver packet loss during authoritative zone propagation coincident with cert rotation -> increased client_hello retries and handshake timeouts. Action items: stagger DNS rollouts, aggressive resolver fallback, add healthchecks/auto-restart for resolver VMs.

eng_dns: followups: replace noisy resolver VM, add CPU healthchecks and auto-restart, add telemetry for SERVFAIL bursts.

Jess: closing thread for now; incident remains open until PR is live. thanks all. :thumbsup:

eng_runtime: (reacted :white_check_mark:) will post when canary healthy.
